verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो गर्भः समभवत् पृथायाः पृथिवीपते। शुक्ले दशोत्तरे पक्षे तारापतिरिवाम्बरे॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Then, O lord of the earth, like the lord of the stars in the heavens, Pritha conceived a son on the first day of the lighted fortnight during the tenth month.
verses.bhavadeepa: आत्मसंस्थां वचनवशामेनां न दूषयामास कन्यात्वस्थापनेनेति शेषः ॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: सा बान्धवभयाद्बाला गर्भं तं विनिगूहती। धारयामास सुश्रोणी न चैनां बुबुधे जनः॥२॥
verses.english: That fair-hipped damsel afraid of the censure of her friends concealed her pregnancy, so that no body was aware of her real state.
verses.bhavadeepa: तत इति । दशोत्तरे एकादशे शुक्ले पक्षे प्रतिपदि चन्द्र झ्व बाल उद्भूतः माघशुक्लप्रतिपदि कर्णनिषेकजन्मेत्यर्थः ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: न हि तां वेद नार्यन्या काचिद्धात्रेयिकासृते। कन्यापुरगतां बालां निपुणां परिरक्षणे॥३॥
verses.english: And as that girl lived in the apartments of maidens, no other women knew her condition except her nurse's daughter who was wellskilled in ministrations.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कालेन सा गर्भं सुषुवे वरवर्णिनी। कन्यैव तस्य देवस्य प्रसादादमरप्रभम्॥४॥
verses.english: (And) in time that damsel of excellent complexion by the favour of that god, Surya, was delivered of a son beautiful as a celestials.

verses.sanskrit: तथैवाबद्धकवचं कनकोज्ज्वलकुण्डलम्। हर्यक्षं वृषभस्कन्धं यथाऽस्य पितरं तथा॥५॥
verses.english: And like his father he was clad in armour, adorned with brilliant golden ear-rings, endued with leonine eyes and bovine shoulders.

verses.sanskrit: जातमात्रं च तं गर्भं धात्र्या सम्मन्त्र्य भाविनी। मञ्जूषायां समाधाय स्वास्तीर्णायां समन्ततः॥६॥
verses.english: And as soon as her delivery took place that girl, in consultation with her nurse, placed her child in a water-proof basket, covered all over with sheets, made of wicker work, smooth, comfortable and furnished with a beautiful pillow. And with tearful eyes she consigned it to the (waters of) the river Ashva.

verses.sanskrit: मधूच्छिष्टस्थितायां सा सुखायां रुदती तथा। श्लक्ष्णायां सुपिधानायामश्वनद्यामवासृजत्॥७॥
जानती चाप्यकर्तव्यं कन्याया गर्भधारणम्। पुत्रस्नेहेन सा राजन् करुणं पर्यदेवयत्॥८॥
verses.english: O king of kings, though she knew that it was not proper for a maiden to be big with child, yet from her affection towards the child she wept bitterly.
verses.bhavadeepa: मधूच्छिष्टं सिक्थकं मयनमितिभाषायाम् । तेन स्थितायां सर्वतो लिप्तायां मञ्जूषायां जलप्रवेशो न भवेदित्यर्थः ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: समुत्सृजन्ती मञ्जूषामश्वनद्यां तदा जले। उवाच रुदती कुन्ती यानिः वाक्यानि तच्छृणु॥९॥
verses.english: And hear the words which Kunti uttered while she, weeping bitterly, consigned the basket to the waters of the river Ashva.

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्ति ते चान्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यश्च पुत्रक। दिव्येभ्यश्चैव भूतेभ्यस्तथा तोयचराश्च ये॥१०॥
verses.english: "O son, may all the creatures inhabiting the firmament, the earth, the celestials regions and the water contribute to your welfare.

verses.sanskrit: शिवास्ते सन्तु पन्थानो मा च ते परिपन्थिनः। आगताश्च तथा पुत्र भवन्त्वद्रोहचेतसः॥११॥
verses.english: May all your ways be auspicious and unobstructed. And, O son, may the minds of those that may meet with you, be not inclined to enmity towards you.

verses.sanskrit: पातु त्वां वरुणो राजा सलिले सलिलेश्वरः। अन्तरिक्षेऽन्तरिक्षस्थः पवनः सर्वगस्तथा॥१२॥
verses.english: On the waters may king Varuna, the lord of waters, protect you. And similarly may Pavana (the wind-god) who ranges in the sky and wanders everywhere protect you in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: पिता त्वां पातु सर्वत्र तपनस्तपतां वरः। येन दत्तोऽसि मे पुत्र दिव्येन विधिना किल॥१३॥
verses.english: O son, may your father, the foremost of those that shed heat and by whom you have been begotten on me by the ordinance of Destiny preserve you everywhere.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्या विश्वे च देवताः। मरुतश्च सहेन्द्रेण दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः॥१४॥
verses.english: And may you be protected by the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sadhyas the Vishvadevas, the Marutas and the cardinal points together with their guardians and Indra.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षन्तु त्वां सुराः सर्वे समेषु विषमेषु च। वेत्स्यामि त्वां विदेशेऽपि कवचेनाभिसूचितम्॥१५॥
verses.english: And may all the gods protect you in every state whether favourable or adverse. Even in foreign countries I shall be able to recognise you on account of your coat-of-mail.

verses.sanskrit: धन्यस्ते पुत्र जनको देवो भानुर्विभावसुः। यस्त्वां द्रक्ष्यति दिव्येन चक्षुषा वाहिनीगतम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Blessed is indeed your divine father, Bhanu, having effulgence for his wealth, who by means of his celestials sight, beholds you going down the stream.

verses.sanskrit: धन्या सा प्रमदा या त्वां पुत्रत्वे कल्पयिष्यति। यस्यास्त्वं तृषितः पुत्रस्तनं पास्यसि देवज॥१७॥
verses.english: And O son of a deity, that lady is also blessed who will adopt you as her son and feed you from her breast when you are thirsty.

verses.sanskrit: को नु स्वप्नस्तया दृष्टो या त्वामादित्यवर्चसम्। दिव्यवर्मसमायुक्तं दिव्यकुण्डलभूषितम्॥१८॥
verses.english: What a dream she has dreamed who will adopt for her son you who are resplendent as the sun, clad in a celestials armour, adorned with celestials ear-rings, endued with broad and expansive eyes like lotuses, possessed of a complexion bright as the copper-coloured lotus-leaves, graced with a beautiful forehead and beautiful hair.

verses.sanskrit: पद्मायतविशालाक्षं पद्मताम्रदलोज्ज्वलम्। सुललाटं सुकेशान्तं पुत्रत्वे कल्पयिष्यति॥१९॥
धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुत्र त्वां भूमौ संसर्पमाणकम्। अव्यक्तकलवाक्यानि वदन्तं रेणुगुण्ठितम्॥२०॥
verses.english: They are also blessed, O son, who will behold you crawl on the ground covered with dust and who will hear your sweet inarticulate speech.

verses.sanskrit: धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुत्र त्वां पुनर्यौवनगोचरम्। हिमवद्वनसम्भूतं सिंहं केसरिणं यथा॥२२॥
verses.english: Having, O king, thus wept long and bitterly, Pritha then consigned the basket to the waters of the river Ashva.

verses.sanskrit: एवं बहुविधं राजन् विलप्य करुणं पृथा। अवासृजत मञ्जूषामश्वनद्यां तदा जले॥२२॥
verses.english: Having, O king, thus wept long and bitterly, Pritha then consigned the basket to the waters of the river Ashva.

verses.sanskrit: रुदती पुत्रशोकार्ता निशीथे कमलेक्षणा। धात्र्या सह पृथा राजन् पुत्रदर्शनलालसा॥२३॥
verses.english: And, O monarch, accompanied by her nurse the lotus-eyed Pritha desirous of beholding her son again and again and overpowered with grief for her son and weeping piteously, at night.

verses.sanskrit: विसर्जयित्वा मञ्जूषां सम्बोधनभयात् पितुः। विवेश राजभवनं पुनः शोकातुरा ततः॥२४॥
verses.english: Laid the basket (on the waters of the Ashva) and entered into the palace with a heavy heart lest her father might know (the secret).

verses.sanskrit: मञ्जूषा त्वश्वनद्याः सा ययौ चर्मण्वतीं नदीम्। चर्मण्वत्याश्च यमुनां ततो गङ्गां जगाम ह॥२५॥
verses.english: (On the other hand) the basket came from the Ashva to the river Charmavati, from the Charınavati to the Yamuna and thence to the Ganga.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गायाः सूतविषयं चम्पामनुययौ पुरीम्। स मञ्जूषागतो गर्भस्तरङ्गैरुह्यमानकः॥२६॥
verses.english: And that basket containing the child, borne along the waves of the Ganga arrived at the city of Champa in the Suta territory.

verses.sanskrit: अमृतादुत्थितं दिव्यं तनुवर्म सकुण्डलम्। धारयामास तं गर्भं दैवं च विधिनिर्मितम्॥२७॥
verses.english: And that child was kept alive on account of the celestials mail and ear-rings both made of Amrita and also on account of the ordinance of Destiny.
